description:
Wayne Gretzky had an incredible start to his NHL career, finishing his first season with at least a share of the League lead in both assists and points. Gretzky’s performance in 1979-80 earned him his first Hart Trophy as MVP of the regular season, beginning a streak of eight consecutive wins and the first of nine career wins. Gretzky scored his first career goal in his third NHL game, tying the game for Edmonton against Vancouver with just over a minute remaining in the third period during a power play, securing a point for the Oilers.

description:
Late in the 1987-88 season, defenseman Brian Leetch joined the New York Rangers and scored his first career goal. Playing at home against the Edmonton Oilers, Leetch skated into the high slot to receive a pass from John Ogrodnick and ripped a slap shot that beat Grant Fuhr, which held up as the game-winner for the Rangers. Leetch went on to capture the Calder Trophy the following season, part of an incredible 18-season Hall of Fame career. In addition to the Calder Trophy, Leetch won two Norris Trophies, a Conn Smythe Trophy, and the Stanley Cup, all with the Rangers.

description:
In just his second NHL game, Mark Messier scored the first goal of his career. Late in the third period, with the Oilers down by a goal, Messier collected the puck behind the net following a strong Oilers forecheck. He threw a backhand pass to the front of the net, where it deflected off a Red Wings defender’s skate and into the net for the game-tying goal. Messier spent the first 12 of his 25 NHL seasons with the Oilers, winning five of his six Stanley Cup championships. Among the other awards he won during his Hall of Fame career were two Hart Trophies and the 1984 Conn Smythe Trophy.

description:
In his fourth NHL game, Paul Coffey scored his first career goal in front of the home crowd in Edmonton. On an Oilers power play, the puck was passed back to the point where Coffey skated to receive it before unleashing a slap shot that ripped past the netminder. Coffey's goal was the first of 396 during his NHL career, which currently ranks second all-time among defensemen in NHL history. The three-time Norris Trophy winner spent the first seven of his 21 seasons in Edmonton, where he won three of his four Stanley Cup championships.

description:
Luc Robitaille, the current all-time goal-scoring leader for the Los Angeles Kings, scored his first NHL goal in his first career game. Playing at home in front of the Kings’ crowd, the play began with a dump-in by Robitaille to start the attack. As the puck was thrown around the boards by the netminder, Marcel Dionne intercepted it and found Robitaille, who headed to the front of the net for a tap-in goal. Robitaille led all rookies during the 1986-87 season in both goals (45) and points (84), earning him the Calder Trophy.

description:
In Mario Lemieux’s highly anticipated NHL debut, he scored his first career goal on his very first shift and first shot on net. Starting in the defensive zone, Lemieux disrupted Ray Bourque's attempt at the blue line, sending the puck into the neutral zone and springing himself on a breakaway. The tall, incredibly gifted centerman showcased his speed and soft hands, racing down the ice and tucking in a backhander. Winning the Calder Trophy, Lemieux completed his rookie season with 100 points, marking the beginning of his magnificent career.

description:
Peter Forsberg won the Calder Trophy during the 1994-95 season, registering 50 points in just 47 games during his rookie campaign with the Quebec Nordiques. In his third career game, Forsberg scored his first goal on a 2-on-1 break against Buffalo. Drafted by Philadelphia with the sixth overall pick in 1991, Forsberg arrived in Quebec as part of the Eric Lindros trade. After the franchise relocated to Colorado, Forsberg went on to win two Stanley Cups with the Avalanche along with the Hart Trophy and Art Ross Trophy.
